en: The *Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Mother of All Stars*, translated by the śramaṇa Facheng at Xudu Monastery in Ganzhou.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Bhagavān was dwelling in the great village of Āṭavī.
All the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and māras;
the sun and moon, Venus, Saturn, other stars, Jupiter, Rāhu, the deity of the comet, and the twenty-eight lunar mansions—all these great assemblies.
They all praised the words of the great vajra vows;
majestic and adorned, they sat together upon lion thrones in a single assembly with the bodhisattvas.
Their names were: the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi,
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrakrodha,
and the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrakula.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajradhanu,
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajreśvara,
and the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrālaṃkāra.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraprabha,
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara,
and the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantadarśin.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Lokamaṅgala,
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Padmāketa,
and the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vipulavaktra.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Padmanetra,
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī,
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Maitreya, and others.
Surrounded before and behind by a great assembly of Bodhisattvas, he expounded the Dharma, which was named "The Vast and Magnificent Array of the Wish-Fulfilling Jewel.
It was excellent in the beginning, middle, and end; its words and meanings were sublime and exquisite; it was unadulterated, pure, and stainless—a holy life (*brahmacarya*).
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, observing the great assembly, rose from his seat.
By his own supernatural power, he circumambulated the World-Honored One hundreds of thousands of times,
prostrated himself, and stood before him holding his own staff.
Assuming the virtuous *paryaṅka* posture, he gazed upon the great assembly;
placing his vajra-palms upon his own heart, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, there are malevolent stars."
The physical form of the punishment is utterly evil and possesses a fierce and sharp mind;
the physical form of the punishment is wrathful and agitates sentient beings,
seizing their vital essence, or seizing their wealth, or seizing their lives.
They cause long-lived sentient beings to become short-lived;
in this way, they afflict and disturb all sentient beings.
It is for the sake of such [beings] that [this was taught].
"I only pray that the World-Honored One will reveal the gateway of the Dharma and protect all classes of sentient beings.
The World-Honored One replied:
Excellent, excellent!
Out of great compassion and for the benefit of all sentient beings,
you have questioned the Tathāgata regarding this profound and secret meaning.
Listen now attentively and reflect well upon it.
I shall explain the methods for subduing malevolent stars when they are provoked to anger,
as well as the secret meanings of making offerings, practicing charity, and performing recitations.
If one performs an offering, one should offer; if one commits an evil deed, one should commit it.
Thus, regarding these stars, their aspects, and so forth—how can they be made to rejoice?
The devas and the asuras, the kinnaras and the nāgas [likewise].
The yakṣas and rākṣasas, humans, and the kāṭapūtanas—
those great deities of fierce majesty and power— how may their wrath be utterly extinguished?
Now, I shall proclaim in due order the secret words and the methods of offering.
At that time, Śākyamuni Tathāgata emitted from his own heart the light of the "Play of Compassion," which entered into the crowns and feet of all the stars.
Immediately, the sun, the moon, and all the stellar deities rose from their seats.
Taking the offerings of the devas, they immediately presented them as an offering to Śākyamuni Tathāgata.
Kneeling with their kneecaps touching the ground, they joined their palms in salutation and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, you have brought benefit to us."
We only pray that the World-Honored One will proclaim a Dharma gate,
so that once we have gathered together, we may guard and protect the teacher of the Dharma;
and that we may attain auspiciousness, remain far removed from blades and staves, neutralize poisons, and establish a boundary of protection.
At that time, Śākyamuni Tathāgata immediately taught the method for making offerings to the stars and the secret words of the dhāraṇī, saying:

Oṃ mūhulakāye svāhā | Oṃ śiṃdhaśabde svāhā | Oṃ lokatāṅgakuṃbhāre svāhā | Oṃ bhoḍe bhoḍe svāhā | Oṃ bhogāsiṣabhoḍe svāhā | Oṃ haṃsurasattame svāhā | Oṃ kṛṣṇaparāṇe svāhā | Oṃ amṛtavidyāye svāhā | Oṃ jātīkṛte svāhā | Vajrapāṇi!
This is the secret heart-mantra of those eight stars;
it is accomplished simply by reciting it.
One should perform the offering by placing it within a twelve-finger-high altar of a single color and fragrance.
One should offer worship by presenting vessels made of clay, copper, gold, silver, or other materials;
for each offering, one should recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times,
O Vajrapāṇi.
Thereafter, recite these secret words of the *dhāraṇī* of the Mothers of the Stars seven times in full;
all the stars will provide protection,
and all poverty shall be completely liberated.
O Vajrapāṇi, if bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, or any other classes of sentient beings find their lives on the verge of ending, they shall obtain long life.
O Vajrapāṇi, if one does not meet with an untimely death after this [text] has reached the ears,
and having established offerings within the maṇḍalas of the various stars, recites it daily;
For that Dharma-preacher, all the stars shall fulfill every wish as desired;
likewise, for those of his kind who are impoverished, all such misfortunes shall be entirely extinguished.
At that time, Śākyamuni Tathāgata immediately expounded for them the Nakṣatramātṛ Dhāraṇī.
He spoke the mantra as follows:
Namo buddhāya.
Namo vajradharāya | Namo padmadharāya | Namo sarvakāraha- [omitted] ||
Namo sarvāśāparipūrakebhyo namaḥ nāśadārebhyo namas taptāśarībhyaḥ.
Tadyathā | medini medini | vṛtra vṛtra | bhañja bhañja ||
Sara sara, pasara pasara,
sambhara sambhara.
Kīṭaye kīṭaye māra māra makṣata makṣata.
Gāḍhaye sarvabijana kuru kuru.
Jin na jin na qi she po ye qi she po ye shan ti e di.
Kṣame kṣamaye tūrṇaṃ dāśaya karmāṇi.
Bhagavati rakṣaya rakṣaya mānava-paripālanam.
King Śarabhadatta Siddhasarvakhaṇḍitakṣatrarāja.
Bhate bhonte bhuvane bhave bhagavati.
Mahāmāye sattvāya tuṣṭimāśaye pabine.
māñcanti mañcanti dūru dūru mañci mūyu mūyu
Svāhā svāhā hāva hāve huṃkari huṃkare tatre putrāye mate.
Manoduḷāna sarvadhātuka atisiddhi.
Samaya svāhā | Oṃ svāhā | Hūṃ svāhā.
Hrīḥ svāhā hūṃ svāhā traṃ haḥ svāhā.
Bhramaṇe svāhā | Acitte svāhā | Sumaye svāhā |
Kharani-sutaye svāhā | Mṛtaye svāhā | Bhūtasi-pataye svāhā.
Ṭaṅkarāya svāhā | kṣaṇavardhanāya svāhā | rāhūbhe svāhā ||
Jvālābhāsa svāhā | Mṛtyu-svāhā | Vajradhara-svāhā |
PAMBO SVĀHĀ | KUMĀRAYA SVĀHĀ | NOKṢATARAṆA SVĀHĀ |
*Sarvauṣadharāṣṭra svāhā | Oṃ sarvabuddhi phaṭ phaṭ svāhā.* Vajrapāṇi,
these are the secret mantra syllables of the Dhāraṇī of the Mothers of the Stars (*Nakṣatramātṛ*).
O Vajrapāṇi, this secret mantra-phrase of the dhāraṇī is the root for accomplishing all matters.
Beginning on the seventh day of the bright fortnight of the ninth month, one undertakes the full poṣadha; then,
having made offerings to the constellations on the fourteenth day,
one maintains the observance until the fifteenth day of the month.
If one can recite and chant it day and night,
for a full nine years, there will be no fear of death,
nor any fear of falling stars or meteors.
Furthermore, there shall be no fear of malevolent lunar mansions, and one will remember past lives.
One will also be able to make offerings to all the stars,
and all the stars will grant them their wishes according to their desires.
At that time, after all the stars had paid homage to the World-Honored One and praised him,
saying, "Excellent!", they suddenly vanished.
*The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Mothers of the Stars*, one fascicle.
